body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Saturday, October 10, and the story leading the day is a big one for local families: an $11.25 billion housing bond is headed to the November ballot, and Kern County's waiting lists show exactly why it matters. Outside, expect a warm one — a high near 86 under mostly clear skies, air quality sitting at a moderate 68, and fire crews still working the Cyrus Fire here in the county.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came early, just after 2:20 a.m., when drivers on both sides of northbound Interstate 5 about two miles south of Taft Highway started dialing in about a crash. The first crew in found one vehicle fully involved in flames and a second off the shoulder, with early reports putting as many as four vehicles in the wreckage and one car left sitting in the center divider. A second ambulance came in from Lamont while firefighters knocked the fire down and units kept working the roadway.

Earlier in the evening, just after 7 p.m., responders were called to a multi-vehicle crash elsewhere in the county where two people were pinned inside a single car — one critical, one moderate. The occupants of the other vehicles were already gone by the time units arrived, and crews called for an extra engine to cut the two patients free.

Shortly before midnight, officers put out an officer safety broadcast after CHP passed along a report of a man with a silver rifle near Highway 99 at Ming Avenue, tied to a white Honda SUV and only about five minutes old. Just before 9 p.m., police and medics went to an apartment at the highest priority for a young child reported not breathing after what was described as a possible bathtub accident, with an engine and ambulance responding together. And a caller on north Chester Avenue reported being assaulted with a firearm behind a business — a man with a handgun had fired it, no one was hurt, and the people who called had left before officers arrived. The rest of the log was grass and vehicle fires from the valley floor out to the eastern county, plus alarms, welfare checks and medical aids.

## Today's weather

It's 72 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 86 and a low around 61 tonight. No active weather alerts are posted for Kern County, and air quality is running moderate at 68 — fine for most folks, though sensitive readers may want to keep an eye on it if you're planning a long afternoon outside. Fire crews remain on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire, so the dry grass and the warm afternoon are worth respecting if you're out in the hills or working equipment near open ground.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that one person was injured after being struck by a vehicle in south Bakersfield.** Police responded to the collision and the injured person was taken for care; details on the circumstances were limited in the initial report. It's a reminder of how quickly a morning walk or a crossing can turn dangerous on busy southside corridors, and we'll pass along more as it comes.

**According to KGET 17, a new veterans center is coming to southwest Bakersfield.** The secretary of Veterans Affairs announced the project, which would expand care and support services for local service members and their families. For a county with a deep military and veteran community, having those services closer to home — rather than a drive out of town — is a meaningful change.

**23ABC reports that California families are still waiting as an $11.25 billion housing bond heads to the ballot.** Voters will decide Proposition 1 on Nov. 3, 2026. The measure would authorize $10 billion for housing programs — affordable rentals, homeownership assistance, supportive housing and preservation of existing affordable units — plus $1.25 billion for CalVet home loans for veterans. In Kern County, the need is outrunning supply: Rebecca Moreno, CAPK's housing director, told the station that for every person they house, three more enter the system. Donnie Singleton applied for low-income housing in 2019; seven years later, she and her daughter are still rotating between a friend's home and her fiancé's, hoping for a two-bedroom she could afford at around $800 a month.

**23ABC also reports that "Operation Safe California" is raising immigration enforcement concerns across the Central Valley.** The Rapid Response Network of Kern said it confirmed sightings beginning October 6, and two days later reported about 61 people detained near Fresno — including people heading to work and at construction sites, shopping centers and gas stations. Immigration attorney Ana Huerta told the station she expects the activity to escalate over the next 45 days. ICE would not confirm the operation, citing operational security, while Congressman David Valadao said DHS told him enforcement is focused on people with active warrants and known criminal histories.

**Keene residents are pushing back against a state effort to place a convicted sexually violent predator in their community, 23ABC reports.** A closed-door court hearing Friday morning could help determine whether William Wilson is eligible for California's Conditional Release Program, which can lead to placement at a rental property in Keene under supervision and a monitored treatment plan. Wilson was convicted twice of sexually abusing two minors in Bakersfield, in 1981 and 1991. Residents Hayley Scott and Joe Martin raised questions about supervision and security. No decision was made Friday; the District Attorney's Office confirms the next placement hearing is set for October 30.

**KGET 17 reports that NOR and Chevron introduced kids to friendly robots at an annual educational playday.** The event gave local children a hands-on look at the technology that keeps the valley's energy industry running — the kind of early exposure that can turn into a career here at home.

## Something good

The new veterans center headed for southwest Bakersfield is worth a smile this morning. For local service members and their families, it means care and support closer to home instead of a long drive out of the county — a real step toward making sure the people who served us don't have to travel far to be looked after. It's the kind of quiet, practical investment that pays off for years.

## Coming up this week

City business picks up Monday with two meetings at noon and mid-afternoon: the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at 12:00, and the Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3:00. Tuesday brings the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee at noon, and Wednesday the Water Board meets at 10:00 — a good one to watch if you follow valley water. The Planning Commission closes out the week's meetings Thursday at 5:30 p.m.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. FANTASIAS takes the stage tonight, October 10. United We Dance brings festival energy on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands October 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour comes through October 18. If you're in a spooky mood, Cults & Classics presents *Psycho* on October 19 — and season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are on sale now.

Have a good Saturday, Bakersfield. Drink some water, keep an eye on your neighbors, and we'll see you tomorrow.

top.title: 1 injured after being struck by vehicle in south Bakersfield, police say
